finding.claim: Schema.concat shares the base exclusiveTests object by reference and then mutates it via test(), polluting the base schema.
finding.title: concat shares and mutates base exclusiveTests

verifier.reason: Concat assigns the base object by reference at schema.ts:311-312, then within withMutation at schema.ts:316-320 calls test() on the mutated combined schema, and test() mutates that object in place at schema.ts:799 via next.exclusiveTests[opts.name] assignment, so the base schema's exclusiveTests is polluted.

repro.expectedBehavior: concat does not mutate or share the base schema's exclusiveTests; adding a non-exclusive test to the base afterwards stacks instead of replacing.
repro.rationale: concat assigns base.exclusiveTests by reference and then test() mutates it when adding the other schema's exclusive test, so the base becomes exclusive and later non-exclusive additions replace instead of stack.
repro.reason: generated test imports paths that are not in the analyzed snapshot: ./src/index.ts

finding.claim: Reference constructor trims the key but checks the original untrimmed key for emptiness, so whitespace-only refs bypass validation.

evidence.snippet:
this.key = key.trim();

    if (key === '') throw new TypeError('ref must be a non-empty string');

finding.title: whitespace ref bypasses non-empty check

verifier.reason: Confirmed: Reference.ts:36 assigns this.key = key.trim() while Reference.ts:38 checks the original key === '', so a whitespace-only key yields an empty this.key without throwing.

repro.expectedBehavior: Whitespace-only ref keys (e.g. '   ', '\t\n') must throw TypeError 'ref must be a non-empty string' after trimming, like the empty string does.
repro.rationale: Reference constructor sets this.key = key.trim() but checks key === '' on the untrimmed input, so '   ' becomes an empty key without throwing. The test records any thrown error and asserts a TypeError was thrown, failing when no error is recorded.
repro.reason: generated test imports paths that are not in the analyzed snapshot: ./src/Reference.ts

finding.claim: validateSync constructs ValidationError with the original input value while async validate uses the validated value, losing cast results on sync errors.
finding.title: validateSync error uses wrong value

verifier.reason: Async validate constructs ValidationError with validated at schema.ts:591, while validateSync receives validated in the same callback but constructs ValidationError with the original value at schema.ts:623, losing the cast result on sync errors.

repro.expectedBehavior: validateSync's ValidationError.value should be the cast/validated value (20, a number) matching async validate, not the original input ('20')
repro.rationale: number().max(10) casts '20' to 20 before failing max; async error carries 20 while buggy sync error carries the original string '20'.

finding.claim: Error sorting matches keys by substring includes instead of exact path segment, so unrelated paths containing the key sort incorrectly.
finding.title: sortByKeyOrder uses substring match

verifier.reason: The code at util/sortByKeyOrder.ts:6 uses err.path?.includes(key) as a substring test with no path-segment or prefix boundary, so paths such as 'address.name' or 'ab' can match an earlier unrelated key like 'name' or 'a' and be sorted by that key's index.
